messages:
ajay: Hey team — after our IdP rotated OIDC keys this morning, one of our SREs can't perform project edits in the console. Buttons are greyed out and direct API calls return 403. Repro steps: 1) Login via SSO 2) Switch to 'acme-prod' org 3) Open Project > Settings — Save button disabled, no client-side network request. If we curl the endpoint we get 403. Sample sanitized curl:
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/9876/settings'

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "permission_denied",
  "message": "caller does not have project.edit"
}
```

maria: thanks — can you paste the response body (you did) and the request headers (no real tokens). Is this affecting everyone in acme-prod or a subset of users? Any recent SSO config changes? :thinking:

ajay: only a subset. We rotated IdP keys early today and our SAML->OIDC bridge was updated. Most users okay, but a few show truncated scopes. Example sanitized headers from an affected user:
```
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
X-Forwarded-For: 10.1.2.3
User-Agent: AcmeCLI/1.2
Scope: openid profile email
```
Previously we saw: openid profile email redwood:project.edit

maya: that scope drop is suspicious. When the bridge re-issues tokens it can alias subject claims; if alias != cached identity key we may not rehydrate role bindings and the authZ cache falls back to a minimal scope set. Quick troubleshooting: have the affected user fully sign out of SSO (clear provider session) and sign in again to get a fresh token. Does that help? :point_up:

ajay: tried sign-out/sign-in — no luck. They still land with limited scope. We have many users so a manual flow isn't ideal. Any server-side workaround?

alex: I'm looking at the auth service logs. When the IdP rotated we got a new issuer-sub mapping and a new token_alias value. Our identity cache key is token_alias + issuer. If the bridge reuses an old alias for the same subject we can end up with two alias entries and stale role bindings. I can force an identity cache invalidation for org=acme-prod which should force re-evaluation of role bindings on next request. Scheduling now.

ops-bot: auth-cache:invalidate requested by alex for org=acme-prod at 6901234578 — job queued and running.

alex: invalidation completed at 6901234586. Please retry the affected user's actions.

ajay: retried — UI Save button is active now and API curl returns 200. Response snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{
  "project_id": 9876,
  "settings": { "feature_x": true }
}
```
Looks fixed for that user. We'll monitor others.

maria: great — marking as resolved for now. Filing internal follow-up to avoid manual cache invalidations: INF-3472 — detect idp key/alias rotation and trigger reactive invalidation for affected orgs + telemetry to catch partial-scope regressions. Thanks for the quick root cause and fix, alex. :white_check_mark:

ajay: Thanks all — please keep me posted if any more users surface the issue.

maya: adding a short KB note for support on this pattern (IdP rotation -> token alias mismatch -> stale authz cache) so on-call can run the invalidate job faster.
